newsitem.title: USA: Northeast suspends nuke training programs.
newsitem.headline: Northeast suspends nuke training programs.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Monday it had suspended indefinitely all training programs at its three Millstone nuclear power plants in Waterford, Conn.
"We ordered a stand-down on all accredited training programs, because of recommendations made by our internal oversight organization," Northeast Nuclear spokesman Rich Gallagher told Reuters.
Northeast's three Millstone plants have been closed for safety reasons since March 1996, and the utility has said it plans to have them ready for restart by early 1998.
Gallagher said it was unclear whether the training suspension might affect the planned restart pace for Millstone 3, the first plant scheduled to be brought back on line.

Previously, Northeast said it anticipated having Millstone 3 ready for restart by the end September, which pending Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) approval, which might put the unit back on line by the end of 1997.
"I don't know that it will have much of an impact, but I would be reluctant to say there will be zero impact," he said.
Northeast Nuclear has scheduled a news conference for 1400 EDT Monday to address the status of training.
It will also comment on Connecticut regulators' ruling last Friday that Northeast may not raise rates to recover $1 billion in Millstone-related costs.
Gallagher said the training programs would be halted "until some improvements can be incorporated into the program." He did not give a time frame.
The suspension of training programs affects all 27 job classifications at the Millstone complex, from security guards to engineers.
